name: Campaign Legal Center
summary: A nonpartisan legal organisation in Washington, founded in 2002 by Trevor Potter, a former chair of the Federal Election Commission. It litigates, files complaints and advocates for the freedom to vote, fair maps, campaign finance law and ethics in government, at the federal, state and local levels, and in 2025 against the administration's executive order on elections. Its 501(c)(4) affiliate, Campaign Legal Center Action, lobbies and keeps its own accounts; gifts to it aren't tax-deductible. In 2025 the Campaign Legal Center spent $21.5 million.

spending.source: https://campaignlegal.org/sites/default/files/2026-06/2025%20Audited%20Financial%20Statement.pdf (audited statement of activities, year ended December 31 2025, p. 6: program $16,005,247 of $21,524,079 total expenses; Campaign Legal Center Action, the 501(c)(4), is not in these statements)
